edge.title: Muon → Muon²: Adam second-moment scaling before NS, lr 0.025→0.10
edge.summary: Starting from #3's baseline, Muon is replaced by Muon²: an Adam-style second-moment EMA v ← 0.95·v + 0.05·g² of the raw gradient divides the Nesterov momentum update elementwise (by √v + 1e-10) before the unchanged 12-step Newton–Schulz orthogonalization and aspect-ratio scaling. Orthogonalization therefore acts on an Adam-normalized direction, with per-coordinate gradient scales balanced first; v needs no bias correction because NS removes the global scale. Keeping #3's wd=0.0125 but raising lr 4x to 0.10 (lr·wd 3.1e-4 → 1.25e-3 per step at peak), it reaches 3.28 in 3325 steps on a single run, 175 fewer than #3.

changes.label: Second-moment scaling before NS
changes.detail: muon_sq_update: momentum.lerp_(grad, 1−mu); v.mul_(beta2).addcmul_(grad, grad, value=1−beta2); update = grad.lerp_(momentum, mu) / (v.sqrt() + eps); then zeropower_via_newtonschulz5 and max(1, rows/cols)**0.5. New state 'v'; beta2=0.95, eps=1e-10, no bias correction.

changes.label: lr 0.025 → 0.10 (wd 0.0125 kept)
changes.detail: optimizer2 = MuonSq(lr=0.10, weight_decay=0.0125): #3's wd with 4x its lr, so the decoupled shrink lr·wd rises from 3.125e-4 to 1.25e-3 per step at peak.

changes.label: train_steps 3500 → 3325
changes.detail: Claimed step equals the scheduled end (no early stop).

changes.label: Inlined hparams; device log; renames
changes.detail: #3's muon_lr / muon_weight_decay constants are replaced by literals in the MuonSq call; adds a print0 of GPU name and world_size; Muon/muon_update renamed to MuonSq/muon_sq_update. Behavior-neutral.

techniques.note: lr 0.10, wd 0.0125, mu 0.95 Nesterov, beta2 0.95, eps 1e-10, NS 12 iters

mechanisms.name: Muon² (Adam-preconditioned Muon)
mechanisms.explain: Alongside the Muon momentum, each hidden matrix keeps an EMA of squared raw gradients (beta2=0.95). The Nesterov momentum matrix is divided elementwise by √v + eps before Newton–Schulz, so orthogonalization is applied to an Adam-normalized direction rather than the raw momentum. Bias correction is unnecessary because NS divides by the Frobenius norm, so only relative per-coordinate scales matter.

caveats: Single run (3.2752, n=1), which does clear the single-run bar (3.28 − 3.2752 = 0.0048 ≥ 0.004). The results folder also ships train_gpt_simple_muonsq.py, rebased on the later #6 skeleton (explicit Gaussian init, zero biases, multi-trial loop, F.rms_norm); the logged run used the old #1/#3 skeleton with torch-default init.
